stories.title: SEC proposes new path for crypto token sales up to $75 million
stories.summary: The SEC has proposed a rule that would let crypto projects raise up to $75 million from investors. The rule would also let projects later end the token's status as a security, CryptoSlate reports.
stories.whyItMatters: A clear exemption path could unlock new US token launches and remove a major legal risk for issuers.
whatToWatch: Publication of formal rule text and a public comment period
Reaction from crypto issuers and securities lawyers
questions: What conditions must a project meet to end a token's securities status?
Would this path apply to tokens already trading today?

sources.title: SEC proposes a path for crypto projects to raise $75 million and later end the token’s securities contract

stories.title: MiCA regulators turn to DeFi vaults, but enforcement won't be easy
stories.summary: EU regulators are starting to look at how MiCA rules apply to DeFi vaults, according to Cointelegraph. The report says enforcement will be hard because vaults are decentralized and lack a clear operator to hold accountable.
stories.whyItMatters: How the EU handles DeFi under MiCA will shape rules for decentralized products beyond centralized exchanges and custodians.
whatToWatch: Formal EU guidance on DeFi vault oversight
How vault protocols respond or adapt their structure
questions: Who would regulators treat as the responsible party for a decentralized vault?
Will vault operators face licensing rules similar to custodians?

sources.title: MiCA is coming for DeFi vaults, but regulation will be difficult

stories.title: Crypto's week: bitcoin and ether bears get squeezed, X eyes stablecoin payouts
stories.summary: CoinDesk's weekly roundup covers a rally in bitcoin and ether that it describes as squeeze-led, hurting short sellers. The roundup also notes a report that Elon Musk's X platform wants to pay creators in stablecoins, among five stories from the week.
stories.whyItMatters: The squeeze shows how short positioning can amplify price swings, and a stablecoin payout plan from X would be a major real-world payments use case.
whatToWatch: Whether X confirms or launches stablecoin creator payments
Whether the bitcoin and ether rally holds as shorts finish unwinding
questions: What specifically triggered the short squeeze?
Which stablecoin would X use, if any?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Ether bears get decimated amid 'squeeze-led' rally and Musk's X wants to pay creators in stablecoins: Crypto's week in 5 stories

stories.title: Instant Bitcoin validation would need 17 GPU-years of compute, study finds
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate report estimates what it would take to validate Bitcoin transactions in 27 milliseconds. The figure: roughly 17 GPU years of compute power, far beyond what typical node hardware handles today.
stories.whyItMatters: The estimate puts a concrete cost on speeding up Bitcoin's validation, a factor in ongoing debates about scaling the network.
whatToWatch: Whether any team pursues GPU-accelerated validation approaches
Follow-on research into cheaper ways to speed up validation
questions: What method produced the 27ms and 17 GPU-year figures?
Would faster validation change tradeoffs around node decentralization?

sources.title: Reaching instant 27ms validation on Bitcoin will take 17 GPU years of compute power

stories.title: Grayscale's Zcash ETF filing sets 2.5% fee, could give DCG a 34% stake
stories.summary: Grayscale has filed for a Zcash ETF that proposes a 2.5% management fee. CryptoSlate reports the filing's structure could leave parent company DCG with a stake of up to 34%.
stories.whyItMatters: A Zcash ETF would test how regulators treat a privacy coin, which has historically faced more scrutiny than bitcoin or ether.
whatToWatch: SEC review and timeline for a decision on the filing
Any pushback over the size of DCG's proposed stake
questions: Why does the filing structure give DCG such a large stake?
Will the SEC treat a privacy coin ETF differently than prior filings?

sources.title: Grayscale’s Zcash ETF filing proposes a 2.5% fee and a potential 34% DCG stake

stories.title: New Illinois rule could tax crypto users on total asset value if brokers miss reporting
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that new Illinois rules could hit everyday crypto users with monthly tax bills based on their total asset value, if a covered broker fails to collect required data. The rule shifts the compliance risk onto individual holders.
stories.whyItMatters: The rule shows how a state-level reporting gap can create large, unexpected tax liabilities for ordinary crypto holders.
whatToWatch: Whether Illinois clarifies or amends the rule after industry reaction
How brokers change reporting practices to avoid triggering it
questions: How would an affected user find out they owe a bill?
Could other states adopt a similar rule?

sources.title: Everyday crypto users face monthly tax bills on total asset value if covered brokers fail to collect under new Illinois rules

stories.title: Zcash jumps 48% past $800 on Grayscale ETF buzz
stories.summary: Zcash rose 48% to trade above $800, CoinDesk reports, as Grayscale's push for a spot Zcash ETF fueled talk of the coin as the 'next bitcoin.' The move follows Grayscale's ETF filing for the privacy coin.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally shows how ETF filing news can move a smaller coin far more sharply than it moves large-cap assets like bitcoin.
whatToWatch: Whether the ETF filing advances toward an SEC decision
Whether the price gain holds once ETF speculation cools
questions: How much of the move is tied to the ETF filing versus broader market momentum?
Is the 'next bitcoin' comparison supported by anything beyond price action?

sources.title: Zcash jumps 48% to over $800 as Grayscale spot ETF push adds to ‘next bitcoin’ buzz

stories.title: BitMart weighs partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after shutdown announcement
stories.summary: Crypto exchange BitMart is considering a partial restart of operations and payouts to creditors, CoinDesk reports, weeks after announcing it would shut down. The report doesn't specify a timeline or the scope of any payouts.
stories.whyItMatters: How BitMart handles creditor payouts matters directly to affected users and could set a template for other exchange wind-downs.
whatToWatch: A formal announcement on restart plans or a payout schedule
The size and timing of any creditor recoveries
questions: What changed since the original shutdown announcement?
How many creditors and how much in assets are affected?

sources.title: Crypto exchange BitMart weighs partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after announcing shutdown

stories.title: Sandbox halts Base and BNB Chain bridging after exploit
stories.summary: Web3 gaming network The Sandbox has paused bridging between Base and BNB Chain after an exploit, CoinDesk reports. The pause is a containment step while the project assesses what happened.
stories.whyItMatters: Bridge exploits remain one of the most common ways attackers drain funds from crypto projects, making incident response here a useful test case.
whatToWatch: Sandbox's disclosure of losses and the exploit's root cause
A timeline for restoring bridging service
questions: How much, if anything, was lost in the exploit?
Will affected users be compensated?

sources.title: Web3 gaming network Sandbox stops Base and BNB chain bridging after exploit

stories.title: Tokenized stocks risk repeating Wall Street's 1960s 'paper crisis,' Fairmint CEO says
stories.summary: Fairmint's CEO argues that tokenized stocks could recreate the settlement backlog Wall Street faced in its 1960s 'paper crisis,' CoinDesk reports. The comparison centers on operational and settlement risk as tokenization grows.
stories.whyItMatters: As interest in tokenized equities grows, unresolved settlement and infrastructure questions could decide whether the market scales safely.
whatToWatch: Whether tokenization platforms address the settlement concerns raised
Any regulatory attention to tokenized securities infrastructure
questions: What specific infrastructure gaps is the CEO pointing to?
Which platforms are most exposed to this risk?

sources.title: Tokenized stocks risk repeating Wall Street’s 1960s ‘paper crisis,’ Fairmint CEO says

stories.title: Solana's first governance vote nears amid a quorum display error
stories.summary: Solana is approaching its first governance vote, but CryptoSlate reports a live display bug showed an incorrect 60% quorum figure. The report indicates the error is in the tracking display, not the underlying vote count.
stories.whyItMatters: A display glitch during a network's first governance vote raises questions about the readiness of its voting tools, even if the count itself is unaffected.
whatToWatch: Whether Solana fixes the display before voting concludes
The final vote outcome and confirmed quorum
questions: Does the display error affect the vote's validity?
What caused the quorum miscalculation?

sources.title: Solana’s first governance vote nears with a live 60% quorum display error

stories.title: AI has made Bitcoin's software a bigger target, security group says
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that a group focused on Bitcoin's core software says AI tools have made the codebase a bigger target for attackers. The group describes ongoing efforts to defend it, though the report doesn't cite a specific AI-driven incident.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's core software underpins the entire network, so new attack methods tied to AI are a systemic risk worth tracking.
whatToWatch: Specific defensive measures the group rolls out
Any disclosed attempts at AI-assisted attacks on the codebase
questions: What concrete AI-enabled threats have actually been observed?
Who funds and staffs this defense effort?

sources.title: AI Has Made Bitcoin Software a Target—This Group Is Fighting Back
